clue.text: Way to make deliveries without going round?

definitions.text: Way to make deliveries without going round?

parts.words: Way to make deliveries without going round?
parts.note: a cricket bowler delivers the ball from one side of the stumps or the other; the side opposite 'round' is the one described

explanation.surface: A courier wonders how to drop off parcels without taking a detour.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler runs in either 'round the wicket' or on the other side of the stumps; 'deliveries' are balls bowled, not parcels.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, bowling from the side nearer the bowling arm is the alternative to bowling round the stumps.

clue.text: Very nasty about Virginia's being lively

indicators.note: the word for very nasty is placed around the state abbreviation, so it wraps it

parts.note: vicious means very nasty
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Someone cruel is surprised to find Virginia full of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a lively person is full of spirit and animation.

clue.text: Very nasty about Come round for a demonstration?

clue.text: Quickly leave work during strike

indicators.note: one piece sits in the middle of the other, as an event within a span of time

parts.note: to hit is to strike
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Workers are urged to walk out fast while the strike is on.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang imperative telling someone to go away at once.

clue.text: The sauce to boast over bum steer?

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for boast is turned over, reading upwards

parts.note: to crow is to boast

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so the letters of steer are scrambled

explanation.surface: Asks whether cheekily bragging about being misled is a bit saucy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses CROW to WORC; 'bum' scrambles STEER to ESTER. A bum steer is US slang for misleading advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Worcester sauce, a spiced condiment, is commonly named after the English city alone.

clue.text: Fellow comes upon piece of furniture that is potentially sought after

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a fellow
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A man stumbles on some furniture that collectors would love.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one could covet is desirable, the kind of thing people would want.

clue.text: Call up woman, originally receiving approval

indicators.note: the first piece takes the second into itself, as a host receives a guest

parts.note: Eve was the original woman in Genesis
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: Someone telephones a woman, who at first agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to summon or conjure a memory or spirit.

clue.text: Wheel's not positioned right on this kind of vehicle

definitions.text: Wheel's not positioned right on this kind of vehicle

parts.words: Wheel's not positioned right on this kind of vehicle
parts.note: the steering wheel sits on the near side rather than the right, as in cars built for driving on the right of the road

explanation.surface: A complaint that a car's wheel has been fitted wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not positioned right' sounds like a faulty fitting, but it means placed on the other side from the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes cars whose steering column is on the left, as in continental Europe and America.

clue.text: Having proper opinions of very rare sort of ruler

explanation.surface: Describes someone sound in their views, like an unusual monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second definition as a king who thinks correctly: a rare thing among rulers, says the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding correct, decent views; and a monarch who reasons well, a rarity.

clue.text: Cover of record incorporating novel variation

indicators.note: the record takes the other letters into its body

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: a variation of the word novel means its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A record sleeve containing a new version of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation' rearranges NOVEL to NVELO, which goes inside EP.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to envelop something is to wrap or surround it completely.

clue.text: Artist and member of string quartet cut short Italian course

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: the instrument loses its final letter, as if trimmed

parts.note: a violin is one of the four instruments in a string quartet

explanation.surface: A painter and a quartet player both finish early to get to an Italian lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Filled pasta pockets served as a course in an Italian meal.

clue.text: Likely to stick with display in bad taste

explanation.surface: A garish display that might also leave you stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: Of paint or glue, slightly sticky; of decor, cheap and vulgar.

clue.text: Progressed in match and finally, at length, completed century

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a tie is a match in a cup competition
went means progressed or moved on

indicators.note: the last letters of the two words that follow are taken

explanation.surface: A cricketer moved on in a long match and reached a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: WENT goes inside TIE; 'finally' takes the last letters of 'at' and 'length', T and H.
explanation.definitionFit: The twentieth is the most recent hundred-year span that has run its full course.

parts.note: the cross-reference points to the entry for outer space; read the answer as a two-word phrase describing that emptiness

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into an article and a noun meaning emptiness, which describes the vastness of the entry at 15.
explanation.definitionFit: Outer space is an empty expanse, an absence of matter.

clue.text: Rocket sent up with velocity could get there

definitions.text: Rocket sent up with velocity could get there

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is written upwards, so it is reversed

parts.note: to rocket is to speed
pace means velocity

explanation.surface: A rocket launched fast enough could reach the far cosmos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' reverses SPEED to DEEPS; the whole clue also describes where a rocket goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The region far beyond Earth's atmosphere, which a fast enough rocket could reach.

clue.text: Table Scot smashed into cell wall

indicators.note: broken into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scotsman crashes a table into a prison cell's wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cell' suggests a prison but is biological.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology, the outer layer of an embryo or the membrane enclosing a cell.

clue.text: Language in neat prose to be edited …

indicators.note: editing reworks text, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tidy writing that still needs an editor's hand.
explanation.definitionFit: An invented international language devised by Zamenhof.

clue.text: … normally exemplifies such use of vocabulary

definitions.text: … normally exemplifies such use of vocabulary

parts.words: … normally exemplifies such use of vocabulary
parts.note: the word normally, carried on from the previous clue, is itself an example of a grammatical class of word modifying a verb

explanation.surface: The sentence from the previous clue continues, saying such usage is typical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'normally' looks like an ordinary word in the run-on sentence, but it is itself the example: a word ending in -ly that modifies a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a word or phrase functioning to modify a verb, as 'normally' does.

clue.text: Complaint involving dog, and little girl's fit of rage

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, so Di's
a temper is a fit of rage

explanation.surface: A dog's illness and a small girl's tantrum in one bad day.
explanation.definitionFit: A viral disease affecting dogs, a canine ailment.

clue.text: Last part of poem? No, I've reconsidered

indicators.note: thinking again puts the letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A poet changes their mind about how to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A short closing stanza of a ballade or similar verse form.

clue.text: Doctor's back to cover vital point, right?

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second as a cover

parts.note: rear means back
gist is the essential point

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a doctor protected an important spot correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a registrar is a senior grade of doctor below consultant.

clue.text: Old physician's written note, after serious case of wind

indicators.note: the note comes after the wind

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind
N is the written abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: An ancient doctor writes up a patient's bad flatulence.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek physician of the 2nd century whose medical writings dominated for centuries.

clue.text: Search for robbers in Winchester?

explanation.surface: Thieves are being sought in an English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack in order to steal; and a Winchester is a make of repeating gun.

clue.text: Swimmer's stroke mostly used at sea

indicators.note: confused, so the letters are rearranged
most of the word, without its last letter

explanation.surface: A swimmer's stroke is mostly used in open water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the E of 'stroke'; 'at sea' rearranges STROK.
explanation.definitionFit: A North Atlantic food fish of the cod family.

clue.text: Beat time (over an hour) ex-schoolmate's taken

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: H is short for hour
R stands for recipe, Latin for take
OB is an old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: An old schoolfriend took more than an hour to keep time.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a throb is a rhythmic pulse or beat.

clue.text: Empty accommodation for sick criminal

indicators.note: the first piece accommodates the second inside it

parts.note: vain means empty or futile
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A vacant house used as a hospital ward for a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicked person, a wrongdoer.

clue.text: Pretend to have secreted gold from overseas

indicators.note: the first piece hides the second within it

parts.note: to feign is to pretend
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone fakes having stashed gold brought from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: coming from another country.

clue.text: Where trousers are firmly secured

parts.note: literally, trousers are held up beneath a strap round the waist; idiomatically, something achieved and safely possessed

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally it is about clothing; the idiom means securely achieved or acquired.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for something gained or achieved and now securely held.
